title: Global-scope handshake
blurb: Canonical WPT-aligned starter checking that ctx.audioWorklet.port is a MessagePort before addModule(), receiving a message posted during module evaluation, echoing text through AudioWorkletGlobalScope, and closing the port.
question: Is ctx.audioWorklet.port a MessagePort before addModule(), can a module post via the global port during evaluation, and does close() stop further replies?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153, AudioWorklet.prototype.port is absent (even with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features and --enable-blink-features=AudioWorkletSharedPort), so the unsupported branch ran and reported audioWorklet.port === undefined with no global-scope message. Spec path not verified in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (unsupported branch verified); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Listeners attached to audioWorklet.port or the global scope port require an explicit close() call to allow resource collection
friction.repro: Open a context, attach a message listener on audioWorklet.port or the global scope port, and drop references without calling port.close().
friction.workaround: Call audioWorklet.port.close() (or port.close() in AudioWorkletGlobalScope) during teardown once no further messages are needed.
